work_packages.title: Prove difficult platform interactions in production routes
work_packages.delivered_outcome: Put the shared Rust document/state model through actual composer, terminal, embedded-browser and native-shell entrypoints. Compare GPUI desktop with Makepad desktop using identical state and content; prove Makepad mobile input, accessibility, extension and browser behavior. Exercise Dioxus DOM/WASM with semantic forms and navigation. A selected target proof is a prerequisite for that target, not platform-wide completion. Start the Cursor and Claude native protocol/SDK replacement proofs early, using controlled fixture and source evidence. A blocker in one provider does not block an unrelated controlled conversation proof, but it blocks full Rust completion for that provider.
mandatory_failure_cases: CJK marked text, UTF-16/byte/grapheme conversion, mixed-direction text, undo and 120k-character drafts where supported.
Rich-document screen-reader navigation, focus return, scaling and keyboard conflicts.
Embedded browser clipping, scrolling, popup/file picker, profile isolation, sandboxing and input focus.
iOS/Android extension lifecycle, process recreation and replacement of mobile OTA/reload assumptions.
A wrapper protocol around a JavaScript SDK is not evidence of a complete independent native provider interface.
acceptance_evidence: Real input-to-presentation traces and semantic accessibility observations on each affected target.
Working integrated browser content and terminal input, including their lifecycle and cleanup.
A candidate decision that accounts for licensing, external browser hosts and generated platform glue.
suggested_agent_ownership: Keep shared text/state contracts under one owner.
Desktop GPUI, Makepad and DOM adapters may be assigned separately once those contracts are stable.

work_packages.title: Submit, stream, approve, interrupt and reopen a conversation
work_packages.delivered_outcome: Implement one real conversation path through Rust command ownership, omdb transaction ownership, a controlled captured provider fixture, bounded publication, shared Rust client state and the selected Rust presentation route. Preserve the existing JSON contract first. Commit events, authoritative projections, receipts, indexes and outbox intent atomically. External effects follow commit. Use only an isolated fresh profile until T05 qualifies native activation of existing profiles. Reuse mapped domain/service internals from native-api-component as migration inputs to the normal application route. Its candidate standalone POST /rpc path is not a replacement product or a substitute for the production WebSocket contract.
mandatory_failure_cases: Disconnect before commit, after commit before acknowledgement and after effect dispatch.
Duplicate command IDs, failed work inside a coalesced batch, approval rejection, cancellation before provider start and interruption during output.
Provider completion followed by late finalization, server restart, stale client cursor and slow subscriber.
No second writer and no retry of an uncertain mutation through another backend.
acceptance_evidence: Exact expected visible output, permissions, event order and receipt/effect behavior.
Submit-to-durable-accept, provider-frame-to-presented-text, acknowledgement-to-effect and reopen-to-current-thread.
Bounded queues, memory, payloads and encode/decode work under concurrent streams.
suggested_agent_ownership: One command/transaction owner and one client-state/presentation owner.
A third owner can maintain controlled transcript fixtures and recovery evidence without editing the shared contract.

dependency_requirements.scope: Exact source identities, fixed fixture/behavior/durability contract, and trustworthy qualification selection for this increment.

Only the input/state/render/lifecycle interfaces used by the selected client/profile. A retained-client control uses its existing production interfaces. A Rust client increment requires the corresponding Rust interface proof. Full mobile extensions, every provider and every target are not prerequisites for this scoped slice.

existing_port_use.native-api-component: Reuse domain/service internals as migration inputs to normal production ingress. Its standalone POST /rpc protocol is not the production WebSocket contract and must not become a second reduced product.

work_packages.title: Negotiate revisioned deltas through commit, replay and rendering
work_packages.delivered_outcome: Add append, replace and splice semantics only through explicit capability/version negotiation. Persist revisions and chunks with their authoritative header. Update durable event/outbox formats where they retain full prefixes. Reuse encoded bytes only for the same authorized wire representation. Keep old-client JSON behavior intact.
mandatory_failure_cases: Missing or mismatched base revision, retained-anchor pruning, reordered/duplicate event, completion replacement and stream gap.
Snapshot recovery during concurrent append and cancellation.
Old/new client-server combinations and downgrade refusal where schemas are incompatible.
Slow subscribers cannot retain unbounded chunks or encoded generations.
acceptance_evidence: Exact reconstructed state after replay, pruning and restart.
Per-turn encoded/stored bytes, allocations, frame latency and bounded retained generations for both negotiated and compatibility paths.
No gain credited to the new protocol when the measured path still writes or sends full prefixes.
suggested_agent_ownership: One owner for protocol and durable representation evolution.
Projection/replay and client application can be separate assignments after schema and recovery rules are fixed.

dependency_requirements.scope: Correct durable JSON-compatible command/stream path for the selected profile.
Required history revision, retained-anchor, snapshot, replay and index interfaces. Completion of every history/UI case and the entire engine comparison is not required to start this increment.

work_packages.title: Navigate, search and manage large histories with the same storage API
work_packages.delivered_outcome: Deliver the requested visible history window, fork ancestry, seek/jump, item detail, exact search, sidebar changes and settings through indexed Rust reads and stable client views. Compare transactional Fjall and direct redb behind omdb against a SQLite control with identical domain operations, representation, visibility and acknowledged durability. At the inspected snapshot, omdb is a pinned redb API/engine fork. A Fjall backend requires a prospective backend contract inside that authoritative boundary. Specify transaction scope, snapshots, commit/acknowledgement sequences, error/unknown-outcome semantics and ownership before changing engines. A generic omdb library change belongs in a separately scoped dependency PR with its own source pin and qualification; T3-specific layouts and adapters stay with their application owners. Record exact omdb/redb/Fjall engine and layout identities in each native generation and qualify conversion, reopen, backup and recovery. There is one authoritative store for a selected profile; no parallel independently committed index/database or drop-in crate substitution is assumed.
mandatory_failure_cases: Sparse/obsolete cursors, nested forks, retries, superseded items, deletion, late parent changes and concurrent new messages.
Unicode offsets, punctuation/identifier ranking, stale search generations, cancelled queries and index rebuild visibility.
Navigation preserves selection, draft, focus and scroll through settings overlays and catch-up.
Compaction and other writers cannot starve foreground reads.

Reject a native generation whose engine/layout/schema identity cannot be opened safely. Engine migration must convert a coherent typed state and preserve its transaction/receipt boundary; incompatible files cannot be reused or silently reopened by another engine.
acceptance_evidence: Exact results, order, rank/ties, snippets, visibility and source offsets.
Page/jump/search-to-stable-viewport latency, records and bytes decoded, physical reads, memory and scroll-anchor error.
Paired engine results under fresh, aged and mixed workloads; no generic SQL-on-redb layer.

A reviewed prospective omdb backend contract and, if needed, a separately pinned/qualified omdb dependency change. Record current omdb fork, direct redb candidate and Fjall candidate identities without calling the omdb fork a crates.io redb build.
suggested_agent_ownership: One owner for visible-order/search semantics and differential fixtures.
Engine adapters can be separate assignments against the same frozen domain API and durability profile.
Client navigation/layout is independently owned after result contracts are fixed.
Generic omdb library work has a separate dependency owner and scoped PR; application owners integrate only a verified pinned result.

Time to usable state/recovery, progress, downtime and peak additional disk.
Documented process-crash, OS-restart and power-loss guarantees verified separately for the declared durability profile.

A fault-injection owner can prepare stage interruption and low-space scenarios against disposable profiles.

dependency_semantics: A dependency requires the named production contract and evidence for the current target/profile increment, not premature closure of the predecessor across all targets. Each package closes only when its own complete applicable scope passes. T16 requires all applicable package and journey scope.
requirements_precedence: The complete full-system architecture and acceptance plan control scope, implementation sequence and performance thresholds. Original journey rows, adverse conditions and behavioral requirements are preserved; historical appendix prescriptions do not override the full-system plan.
